questions.prompt: A repo has an `AGENTS.md` with all the conventions, and no `CLAUDE.md`. A teammate adds a `CLAUDE.local.md` to keep their own notes. What happens to `AGENTS.md`?
options: Nothing — `CLAUDE.local.md` is personal and ignored for loading decisions
Claude stops reading `AGENTS.md`, because `CLAUDE.local.md` counts as a `CLAUDE.md`
Claude reads neither, because the files conflict
questions.explanation: The presence check treats `CLAUDE.local.md` as a `CLAUDE.md`, so adding one suppresses `AGENTS.md` by default. Option 0 is the tempting wrong answer because 'local' sounds excluded from decisions — but it counts, which is exactly the trap.

questions.prompt: You want Claude to read both your `CLAUDE.md` and your `AGENTS.md`, in each directory, without merging them yourself. What do you change?
options: Nothing — Claude reads both by default
questions.explanation: The Project instructions setting selects `claude-md-and-agents-md`, which reads each directory's `CLAUDE.md` first and its `AGENTS.md` after. Option 0 is tempting because the import works, but it makes `AGENTS.md` load *through* `CLAUDE.md`, which is the opposite of reading both as separate files.

questions.prompt: A teammate on Windows clones your repo. Their `CLAUDE.md` is one line that points at `AGENTS.md` instead of holding the instructions. What most likely happened?
options: The `CLAUDE.md` was committed as a symlink, and Git checked it out as a plain text file
Claude Code stripped the file because it conflicted with `AGENTS.md`
Their version of Claude Code is too old to read `AGENTS.md`
questions.explanation: A committed symlink needs Developer Mode or Admin on Windows, and Git checks it out as text unless `core.symlinks` is enabled, leaving a one-line file. Option 3 is tempting because `AGENTS.md` support is version-gated — but the symptom is a truncated `CLAUDE.md`, which points at the symlink, not the version.

questions.prompt: You keep personal test credentials in `CLAUDE.local.md` and work across two worktrees of the same repo. You open the second worktree and the file is gone. Why?
options: Claude deleted it because it was gitignored
A gitignored `CLAUDE.local.md` exists only in the worktree where you created it
`CLAUDE.local.md` only loads in the repository root, not in worktrees
You need to set Project instructions to `claude-md` first
questions.explanation: Because it is gitignored, the file is not carried into a new checkout, so each worktree needs its own. Option 2 is tempting because 'root only' sounds like a loading rule — but the real cause is that the file was never copied, not that loading is scoped.
